standard_prerequisites.name: Transport in a fibration
standard_prerequisites.statement: Along a path between two points of the base, the fibres of a type family are related by transport, and the transport along reflexivity is the identity.
standard_prerequisites.use: The encoding map is defined as transport of the given point of the fibre at the base point.

standard_prerequisites.name: Path induction
standard_prerequisites.statement: To prove a family of statements about all paths out of a point it suffices to prove the case of the reflexivity path.
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the second round-trip identity to a single statement at the base point.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-inverses and equivalences
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map is an equivalence as soon as it has a two-sided inverse up to homotopy.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof exhibits the decoding map as the inverse of the encoding map on the loop space.

core_obligations: Define the encoding map from paths out of the base point to the fibres by transporting the given point of the fibre at the base point (source lines 2585-2589).
Show that the composite of encoding after decoding at the base point is the identity, which is the third hypothesis of the statement (source lines 2590-2592).
For the other composite, state the pointwise identity to be proved for every path out of the base point (source lines 2592-2595).
Reduce that identity by path induction to the base point, compute the transport there, and conclude with the fourth hypothesis (source lines 2596-2599).

proof_roadmap.step: Define encoding by transport and exhibit the two composites.
First composite: exactly the third hypothesis.
Second composite by path induction, reducing the transport to the fourth hypothesis.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 2571-2582: under a fibration with a point of the fibre at the base point, a decoding map and two equations, the loop space at the base point is equivalent to that fibre. The proof (source lines 2584-2600) is not a pointer: it defines the encoding map as transport of the given point along the path, then exhibits the decoding map as its two-sided inverse. One round trip is exactly one of the two hypotheses, and the other is stated pointwise for every path out of the base point and reduced by path induction to a single identity at the base point, where the transport computes and the second hypothesis applies. The definition of the encoding map and the reduction of the second round trip are the substance, and the statement alone does not display them.
